Kvedarna Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tauragės apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Kvėdarna holds one of the most significant rabbinic connections documented in this collection: Rabbi Avraham Yeshayahu Karelitz (1878–1953), known as the Chazon Ish and among the most influential Orthodox halakhic authorities of the 20th century, studied for many years in the local beit-midrash. R. Moshe Rosen, author of Nezer HaKodesh, served as the community's rabbi in the early 20th century. The Jewish population reached 671 (56 percent) by 1897. After the 1941 German invasion, Jewish males over 15 were taken to the Heydekrug (Šilutė) labor camp, with those unfit for work periodically executed and the rest dying at Auschwitz or in the Warsaw Ghetto; women and children were murdered by Lithuanians that autumn. The local Catholic priest hid the community's Torah scrolls and returned them to the few Kvėdarna Jews who survived.
